speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Government currently audits the financial viability and operational sustainability of Student Care Centre (SCC) operators; (b) if so, how are such audits conducted; and (c) whether the Government intends to improve its governance processes over SCCs to avoid future abrupt closures, to reduce the risk of disruptions to children, parents, and staff.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
text: asked the Minister for Education in relation to the interim plan for the Ministry’s schools and teachers to continue student care centre operations following the abrupt closure of private student care centre operator in February 2026, how does the Government plan to recognise these extra efforts and ensure that the Ministry’s teachers are not further overworked.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what regulatory safeguards are in place to ensure continuity of student care centres when they cease operations abruptly; (b) whether there are framework level requirements on financial governance, contingency planning and parent fee protection; and (c) how the Ministry assesses operator resilience to minimise disruption to students, parents and staff.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
text: asked the Minister for Education in relation to the abrupt closure of Little Professors student care centres, how the Government plans to assist in the recovery of salary payments due to staff and the recovery of GIRO payments unfairly deducted from parents.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Our schools have stepped in to provide interim after-school support.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: School staff have been deployed on a rotational basis to bridge the gap since the incident first happened.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Over the past three weeks, schools have engaged relief manpower, including retired school staff, flexi-adjunct teachers and external instructors, to fill the staffing needs and to reduce the need for continued deployment of school staff.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Parent support groups in some schools have also stepped in to provide additional support.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOE headquarters (HQ) officers have been providing onsite assistance and have helped to relieve the administrative load on schools.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: All affected schools have been able to continue providing after-school care for students.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I know that the children and their families are also appreciative of the care and concern.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: School staff who have put in additional contributions during this interim period will be recognised.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We want the new operators to start as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOE and schools have also been able to employ and pay former LPLC staff in their original centres if they are keen to do so, until a permanent operator is appointed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This will provide some financial stability for these affected staff in the interim, while they continue to care for our students.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Affected LPLC staff have also been advised to reach out directly to the Ministry of Manpower, the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management or the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board to file claims for unpaid salaries and CPF contributions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We had at that point also advised affected parents to cancel their GIRO arrangements immediately and to consider filing a claim with the Small Claims Tribunal.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As police investigations are ongoing, I am not able to comment further on this issue.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Pending the outcomes of police investigations, we will work with relevant agencies to see how we can further support parents.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Members have asked about our selection and monitoring mechanisms for SCC and KCare operators.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As part of the selection process, operators have to demonstrate adequate financial standing before they are considered.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: After they are appointed, MOE and schools maintain oversight over operators and monitor their performance in terms of how well they are providing the SCC and KCare services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These monitoring processes are reviewed regularly so that we can continue to improve our safeguards.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We also value parents’ direct feedback about our SCC and KCare centres so that issues can be addressed in a timely fashion.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Today, parents can provide feedback to SCC and KCare staff, to the schools, and directly to MOE.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In 2025, MOE directly received a total of 212 emails and phone calls providing feedback on SCCs and KCare centres.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We reviewed all of them and followed up with the schools and operators when needed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Before this incident with LPLC, MOE has not had cause to terminate the services of any school-based SCC and KCare operator.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Nevertheless, we do recognise that there is room for improvement within the sector to provide better services, to strengthen the resilience of operators and to better monitor the service provision.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are further reviewing our processes for selecting and monitoring SCC and KCare operators.
Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar): Thank you, Mr Speaker.
First, I declare that I am the advisor to the Education Services Union that looks after the affected teachers.
Second, I declare that I am the advisor to the Singapore Teachers Union that looks after the teachers who stepped in to help.
And third, I declare that Hong Wen school, which is one of the affected schools, is in my constituency.
And to that end, I asked not one, not two, but three Parliamentary Questions (PQs) on the matter.
When I visited Hong Wen school the day after the closure, I was glad to see the parents' support group and the teachers coming in to make sure the kids had the continuity of care.
They told me that the incident was regrettable, but possibly preventable.
So, my two supplementary questions, Mr Speaker, are about how we can prevent these incidents from happening again.
First on MOE's due diligence, both before an operator is appointed and during the operations.
What levels of safeguards can we expect MOE to implement to ensure that operators with financial standing are appointed?
And during operations, that they continue to be in good financial standing, so that we are assured of the sustainability of the operations.
This is conceptually no different from how other Government procurement entities, such as those in the built environment sector, look at the largest contractors and vendors of the Government.
The second and final question is on MOE's whistle-blowing policies.
Because parents in our Whampoa and Boon Keng estates told me that they had given feedback about the deteriorating quality of the SCC last year.
So, when MOE said that they only found out about it in February this year, the parents told me that this did not gel with the feedback they had given.

Whistle-blowing allows us to have this early signal, so I hope that MOE could also consider how we could look at early signals to avoid a situation where MOE and parents and children and staff are caught off guard in the future.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On his first question about due diligence, the levels of safeguards associated with the financial standing of the operator – these are assessed at the point of the application, the tender, when the operator submits a tender to have the licence to operate the centre at the schools.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do indeed have a series of items that we look at, including the capitalisation of the company, the financial reserves, the depth of their governance and so forth.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: He is asking then about whether we have means to do so during the course of the operations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so then, we continue to have oversight of this process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We await the investigations as to what happened in this incident and we will see whether there are lessons learnt that will inform us about whether we need to put in further mechanisms, going forward.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On whistle-blowing, indeed, we do have a variety of channels.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: One of the affected schools, Westwood Primary, is also in my constituency.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I want to thank the staff and the volunteers for stepping up in this uncertain period.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I ask these questions in the spirit of improving the systemic resilience of the sector, the first one being: will the Ministry include a review of its current operators and consider a strategic partnership to have a whitelist of operators that could step in if one ceases to operate, so that we do not have to activate our teachers, who already have increased workload?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The second one alludes to the same early warning trigger system that hon Member Shawn Loh mentioned earlier: whether we can have a broader view of some of these triggers which could include both operational and financial aspects?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: For example, if a centre rapidly expands across the island, or if we see that staff are being laid off, on top of just the routine reporting that these centres currently do.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And thirdly, are there ways to also ensure that parents' fees are also safeguarded?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Most of the parents who came to see me in my Meet-the-People Session were truly worried about recovery of their deposits.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Could we weave in, perhaps one of the factors could be ring-fencing parents' fees or deposits in a client's account or by way of some form of an insurance that the providers could purchase to protect parents' deposits?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are reviewing, not just this incident, but the sector as a whole and we do want to improve.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We want to improve the resilience of the operators within the sector.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We want to improve the service provision for our students and we want to improve parents' confidence in the operators and the care that their children are receiving.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Member had made a couple of suggestions.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The first, in terms of systemic resilience, looking at some form of whitelist or strategic partnership with an operator or operators.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And the idea that perhaps, we might develop capability in partnership with an operator so that there is a systemic resilience, not just an operator resilience, should another incident occur, whether we would have the capability then to rely on such an operator to step in, and not only on the MOE staff and the parent support groups, and all the other people who helped.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: He suggested another set of ideas about operational and financial monitoring of the operators to pick up in advance, if such a thing occurs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Actually, in general, MOE and the schools work very closely with the operators.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have ongoing discussions, we know the staff very well, we integrate on some programmes and services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There have been issues over the years that we have had to deal with.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some operators, maybe staff are sick or face staff shortage, or perhaps the business issues that we have to think about.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For most of the operators, we actually have a fairly close relationship, and hence, we have not had an anxiety about whether we were not aware about what was happening within the operator.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I take his point that perhaps, we need a mechanism to give us systemic confidence that we have sight into the finances and operations, such that we would have an early warning, if there was a resilience issue of a given operator.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are studying the sector and we will see if we can find ways to introduce such mechanisms, including, for example, how an operator manages their staff; which I think is something that we have to take very seriously.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: His third suggestion about the parents' fees, indeed, that is an anxiety that many parents will have about the deposits that they have paid.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And then now, for many parents, there is the issue of the deposits that they have paid, which they have not been able to claim back yet.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The matter is still under investigation and we will see how best we can assist those parents, and then see what is the appropriate mechanism going forward to restore parents' confidence in the operators in this space.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I know you have filed a PQ on this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My question has to do with the pursuit of recourse by many of these.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand that Senior Minister of State mentioned that the way that they should proceed is by going to the Small Claims Tribunal.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I have also raised the concern whereby the teachers are now given extra load to do interim supervisory duties.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: How will MOE ensure that such stopgap measures do not become normalised or prolonged, such that it affects their workload?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And how can we make sure that those teachers who are currently on those workloads are recognised formally and they can be added into the additional responsibilities?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I express my deep appreciation for the teachers who have indeed stepped in to care for the students.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do recognise that this is in addition to their workload and that will be recognised by the schools as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The operational way in which we relieve that workload will vary from site to site.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The principals and the site conditions of, for example, the Little Professor staff who have chosen to stay on, or external staff who have been able to come in – means that it is not exactly the same from site to site.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, exactly what the teachers have to do and the intensity of the workload will vary.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have to take an operational approach, but our intent is indeed for the teachers then to focus on their primary duties and where possible for us then, to relieve them of these duties.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And I once again would very much like to thank them for that.
